content: 1. Reduce the dose of eluxadoline to 75 mg orally twice daily if co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. Monitor the patient closely for any adverse effects. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 3. Elvitegravir, a CYP3A4 substrate, may have increased levels when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for potential toxicity. 4. Co-administration of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with clarithromycin can lead to increased drug levels due to CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Omeprazole may have a minor effect on elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels and effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administered with clarithromycin or omeprazole. 8. Clarithromycin and encorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 9. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 10. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 11. Clarithromycin increases the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, avoid entrectinib, as it is a CYP3A4 substrate. 13. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of enzalutamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels of enzalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and epinephrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Clarithromycin and eribulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor the QT interval with ECG. 21. Omeprazole decreases the levels of erlotinib by altering its absorption. Co-administration is contraindicated. Avoid using proton pump inhibitors with erlotinib. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Clarithromycin and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Clarithromycin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Omeprazole increases the levels of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin and escitalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels of eslicarbazepine acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for gastrointestinal symptoms. 35. Omeprazole increases the levels of estazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels of estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels of estrogens conjugated synthetic by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels of estrogens esterified by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels of eszopiclone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day and monitor closely. 42. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels of etoposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Clarithromycin and ezogabine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, particularly when ezogabine is titrated to higher doses. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust the fedratinib dose accordingly. 50. Clarithromycin increases the levels of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential hypotension, edema, bradycardia, or acute kidney injury. 52. Clarithromycin increases the levels of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed.
